title: Beauty, Barbering & Salon Business
tagline: Hygiene and Dubai salon rules, skin and hair science, cutting and colour basics, and running a profitable salon or chair.

superpower.name: Salon Star
superpower.description: Looks the part and runs a busy chair: more from beauty jobs and better confidence.

syllabus: Week 1: Hygiene, safety and Dubai salon rules
Week 3: Cutting, fades and colour basics
Week 4: Pricing, rebooking and running a salon

weeks.title: Hygiene and Salon Rules
weeks.objective: Keep every client safe with proper sterilisation and meet Dubai's salon requirements.

slides.title: Clean, Disinfect, Sterilise
slides.body: Salons handle skin, hair and sometimes blood. Infections spread through dirty tools, so every tool is cleaned and disinfected between clients, and metal tools that can break skin are sterilised.
bullets: Clean: wash off hair and debris with soap and water
Disinfect: soak in a hospital-grade disinfectant for the full contact time on the label
Sterilise: autoclave metal tools that can cut skin (about 121°C for 15 to 20 minutes)
Single-use: razor blades, files and buffers go in the bin after each client
slides.takeaway: Every client gets clean tools, every time, no exceptions.

slides.title: Dubai Salon Requirements
slides.body: Beauty salons and barbershops in Dubai are licensed and inspected by Dubai Municipality. Staff need occupational health certificates and hygiene training, and inspectors check sterilisation, records and cleanliness.
bullets: Licensed premises and trained staff
Health certificates for workers who touch clients
Sterilisation records and a clean, separated tool area
A new blade for every shave
slides.takeaway: Inspection-ready every day means clients feel safe every day.

lab.title: Hygiene Audit Lab
lab.brief: Audit a workstation: list every tool, how it's cleaned, disinfected or sterilised, and fix any gaps.
lab.proTip: Show clients you open a fresh blade: it builds instant trust.

caseStudy.scenario: A client is in a hurry and asks you to reuse the blade from the last client. What do you do?

options.explanation: Shared blades can spread blood-borne infections.

options.text: Politely refuse and open a new blade: it takes seconds.
options.explanation: A new blade every client is both safe and required.

options.text: Rinse it under the tap and reuse it.

quiz.question: Which tools must be thrown away after each client?

weeks.title: Skin and Hair Science
weeks.objective: Understand skin types, hair structure and how to avoid reactions.

slides.title: Skin Types and Care
slides.body: Good beauty work starts with reading the skin: its type, its sensitivity and how it reacts to the sun. Dubai's strong sun makes sunscreen part of every routine.
bullets: Skin types: normal, dry, oily, combination, sensitive
Fitzpatrick scale I to VI: how skin reacts to sun
Daily sunscreen SPF 30 or more
Refer clients with rashes or lesions to a dermatologist
slides.takeaway: Treat the client's actual skin, not a standard routine.

slides.title: Hair Structure and Patch Tests
slides.body: Hair has three layers: the cuticle (outer scales), cortex (strength and colour) and medulla (core). Chemical services change the cortex, so they can damage hair or cause allergic reactions.
bullets: Porosity: how well hair absorbs moisture and colour
Patch test 48 hours before any hair dye, every time
Strand test before colour or lightening
Bleach and heat break bonds: use bond builders and heat protection
slides.takeaway: A 48-hour patch test is a small step that prevents a serious reaction.

lab.title: Consultation Lab
lab.brief: Run a full consultation: skin or hair type, history, allergies, goals and a patch-test plan.
lab.proTip: Write everything down: records protect your clients and you.

caseStudy.scenario: A walk-in wants a full hair colour today and has never been coloured before. What's right?

options.explanation: Without a patch test an allergic reaction could be severe.

options.text: Do a patch test now and book the colour for at least 48 hours later.
options.explanation: The 48-hour patch test checks for allergies safely.

options.text: Use double the developer to be quick.

quiz.question: How long before dyeing should a patch test be done?

weeks.title: Cutting, Fades and Colour
weeks.objective: Learn the core cutting and fade techniques and how colour works.

slides.title: Clipper Guards and Fades
slides.body: A fade blends from very short at the bottom to longer on top. Clipper guard numbers set the length.
bullets: #0: no guard (about 0.5 mm)
Blend in sections from shortest to longest, with the lever and a flicking motion
Check symmetry from behind and in the mirror
slides.example:
A mid skin fade:
• Bottom: #0 up to just above the ear tip
• Next band: #1, then #2 a little higher
• Blend into #3 at the parietal ridge, leaving the top for scissors.
Work the lever (open and closed) between guards to remove lines.
slides.takeaway: Smooth blending is what separates a fade from a line of steps.

slides.title: Colour Basics
slides.body: Hair colour is measured in levels from 1 (black) to 10 (lightest blonde). Developer strength controls how much the hair lifts.
bullets: Levels 1 to 10, black to lightest blonde
Developer: 10 vol (deposit only), 20 vol (1 to 2 levels of lift), 30 vol (2 to 3), 40 vol (3+; use with care)
Colour can't lighten colour: going lighter over dyed hair needs lightener
Toner neutralises unwanted warmth (purple cancels yellow)
slides.takeaway: Know the starting level and the target before you mix anything.

lab.title: Practical Lab
lab.brief: On a training head, do a mid fade and a colour plan for a client going from level 4 to level 7.
lab.deliverable: Photos of the fade and a written colour formula.
lab.proTip: Practise on mannequins until the blend is invisible from arm's length.

caseStudy.scenario: A client with level 5 dyed hair wants to be level 8 using a box dye. What do you explain?

options.text: Box dye will lift it fine.
options.explanation: Colour doesn't lighten existing artificial colour.

options.text: Existing colour needs a lightener, then a toner; it may take more than one session to protect the hair.
options.explanation: Lift with lightener, tone, and protect the hair's condition.

options.text: Use 40 vol on the whole head immediately.
options.explanation: That risks breakage and scalp irritation.

quiz.question: Which colour cancels yellow tones?
quiz.explanation: Purple is opposite yellow on the colour wheel.

weeks.title: Running a Salon or Chair
weeks.objective: Price services, rebook clients and grow.

slides.title: Pricing Services
slides.body: Price from your time, products and overheads, then check the local market.
bullets: Service price = time × hourly rate + product cost
Know your break-even: rent, licence, staff, products
Premium services (colour, treatments) carry the margin
Retail products add income and help results at home
slides.example:
Pricing a men's fade with beard trim:
• 45 minutes at AED 120 an hour = AED 90
• Products and blade: AED 8
Price: about AED 100, with a 'cut + beard + hot towel' package at AED 130.
slides.takeaway: Price for profit, not just to be the cheapest.

slides.title: Rebooking and Reputation
slides.body: A full diary comes from clients who come back. Rebook before they leave, follow up, and protect your reviews.
bullets: Rebook at checkout: 'Same time in 3 weeks?'
Reminders by WhatsApp a day before
Ask happy clients for a review
Before-and-after photos (with consent) for social media
slides.takeaway: The easiest client to book is the one already in your chair.

lab.title: Salon Business Lab
lab.brief: Price a menu of 8 services and plan how you'll fill a 40-appointment week.
lab.deliverable: A price list with costs and a rebooking plan.
lab.proTip: Track your rebooking rate: aim for most clients leaving with their next appointment.

caseStudy.scenario: A client is unhappy with their haircut. What's the professional response?

options.explanation: Arguing loses the client and their friends.

options.text: Listen, apologise, and offer a free fix right away or at a time that suits them.
options.explanation: Fixing it kindly often turns an unhappy client into a loyal one.

options.text: Charge them for a new cut.
options.explanation: Charging to fix your work damages trust.

quiz.question: Service price is roughly:
quiz.explanation: Time plus products, then check the market.
